checks.result: The closure of the rational graph in E0^(2r) x P1 is integral and projective. Choose a symmetric ample product bundle with projectively normal embedding, for example sufficiently ample complete factors and their Segre product. This meets the publication setup; replacing a height by its fixed positive multiple or boundedly equivalent representative only changes fixed constants.

The coordinatewise group generated by P1 in r coordinates and P2 in r coordinates is fixed and finitely generated before labels are chosen. Actual paired labels lie in its subgroup. Taking perturbation b=0 places every such point in C(Gamma,epsilon). Constants do not depend on n_i or m_i.

Reused no-translate conclusions exclude exactly the required positive-dimensional abelian translates. A translate in the closed graph fiber through a point in the rational-map domain has a dense open part on which the rational function is constant. Boundary points elsewhere do not invalidate this implication.

The product canonical height is a fixed positive multiple of the sum of coordinate heights. Pointed elliptic isomorphisms and conjugation preserve the chosen normalized canonical heights. With m_i=n_i, this sum is twice the original sum; division by two changes constants only.

Here r=4, E0^8 is fixed and the labels n,a,t,b are all nonzero. Sum no-translate permits these without oddness. Replacing half-trace by quarter-trace costs at most log2 in absolute logarithmic height. Since hat h([n]P)=n^2 hat h(P) and hat h(P)>0, B^2 is bounded by the coordinate sum divided by this fixed positive constant, giving the displayed M1 h(T)+M2. Increasing M2 to at least1 is harmless.

The product application additionally requires odd labels as expressly stated. The many-block application uses the same fixed coordinatewise subgroup construction and relies on its separately stated no-translate hypotheses. No new acceptance of those geometric proofs is made here.

The geometric slope can be effective after fixed embedding/height choices. The additive constant is only existential; all resulting M0/M2 remain independent of labels but are not computed. Nothing in this application supplies an effective defining N0.
